title: Parents wanted college; Mrs. Allen's Tuskegee and Fisk connections
summary: He told his parents after leaving; they wanted him in college, and Mrs. Allen could send promising pupils to Tuskegee or Fisk.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, what about your parents when you told them you were going on the boat? What did they think about that?
Or did you go first and then let them know?
Yeah, I let them know later. Let them know later. I don't think I would have got out of there.
They wouldn't have went for it, because
they wasn't for me -- after I got up, they wasn't for me playing music. They were for me going to college. Wanted me to go to school, you know.

Go to college and then this woman had great connections, Mrs. Bessie Allen, the woman who had the band. If you showed any kind of promise, you know, not only music, but character or something, and you wanted to go to school, she had connections where she could send you to Tuskegee, one of the -- you know, the black universities Tuskegee or Fisk, something like that.
Because some of them did go, you know, some of them didn't play music after they got up to a size where they could go to college. Instead of staying with music they went to college, you know.
Yeah, and got into something else, you know.
Wonderful woman. I'll never forget her. And so now we sent our horns back. Now we feel safe.
